lesson.text: Quick memory: when your team has the ball, are you attacking or defending? (Attacking.) Today: how to keep the ball, find space and defend a goal.
In invasion games, two teams invade each other's half to score in a goal or an end zone. Football, netball, basketball, hockey and rugby are all invasion games.
Keep the ball: pass to a teammate who is free, not one who is marked. Call their name, then pass firmly and straight, with a chest pass, a bounce pass or an overhead pass.
Find space: when a teammate has the ball, move away from the player marking you into an empty space, and call for it. After you pass, move again: pass and move! Here, B is in space.
Defend: when the other team has the ball, mark a player. Stay close, between them and the goal you defend, watch the ball and try to intercept a pass. Never grab or push.
Width and depth: attackers spread out across the pitch, and some stay behind the ball. That stretches the defenders and makes gaps to pass through.

Every game has its own rules. In netball you may not run with the ball, and must pass it within 3 seconds. In basketball you dribble by bouncing it. In football, only the goalkeeper may handle the ball, in their area.
Try it in the world: build a pitch with two goals and play 3 against 3 with friends in a park. Pass and move, find space, and mark a player when you defend.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is an invasion game?
exercises.hint: In which game do two teams try to get into each other's half to score?
exercises.explain: Netball: two teams try to score in each other's goal. Rounders is striking and fielding, tennis is a net game.

exercises.prompt: When your team has the ball, you are defending.
exercises.explain: False: with the ball, your team is attacking. Without it, you defend.

exercises.prompt: Your teammate has the ball. What should you do?
exercises.hint: How can your teammate pass to you safely?
choices: move into a space and call for it
exercises.explain: Move away from defenders into a space and call for the ball, so your teammate can pass to you.

exercises.prompt: Your team is blue and has the ball. Which teammate is free to pass to?
exercises.hint: Look for the blue letter with no red square close by.
exercises.explain: B: every red player is far from B. A and C each have a red player right beside them.

exercises.prompt: Match each pass to how it travels.
exercises.hint: The name of each pass tells you where it goes.
exercises.explain: A chest pass goes straight from your chest, a bounce pass bounces once, and an overhead pass goes high over a defender.

exercises.prompt: When you mark a player, you stay between them and the goal you are defending.
exercises.hint: Where would the attacker want to go?
exercises.explain: True: between the player and your goal, so they cannot run or pass straight to it.

exercises.prompt: In netball, what are you not allowed to do?
exercises.hint: Think of the netball rule about moving.
exercises.explain: You may not run with the ball in netball: you must stop and pass it within 3 seconds.

exercises.prompt: Put pass and move in order.
exercises.hint: You have to see a teammate before you pass.
items: look up for a free teammate
exercises.explain: Look up, pass, move into a new space, then call for the ball back.

exercises.prompt: Why do attackers spread out across the pitch?
exercises.hint: What happens to the defenders when attackers spread out?
choices: to stretch the defenders and make gaps
to stay out of the game
to make the pitch look full
so they cannot hear each other
exercises.explain: Spread out, the attackers pull the defenders apart, which makes gaps to pass through.

exercises.hint: Which ones do you do when your team has the ball?
exercises.explain: Attacking: finding space, shooting, calling for the ball. Defending: marking, intercepting, blocking the way to goal.

exercises.prompt: You are blue and the red team has the ball. Which red player is free, so a blue player should mark them?
exercises.hint: Find the red letter with no blue circle close by.
exercises.explain: B: no blue player is near B, so B could get an easy pass. A and C are already marked.

exercises.prompt: A good defender pushes the attacker to get the ball.
exercises.hint: What does the lesson say about grabbing or pushing?
exercises.explain: False: pushing or grabbing is a foul, and the other team gets a free pass. A good defender stays close, between the player and the goal, and tries to intercept the ball.

exercises.prompt: Your team loses the ball to the other team. What should everyone do?
exercises.explain: The other team is attacking now, so your whole team defends straight away: find a player to mark.

exercises.prompt: A netball team has 7 players on court. Two teams play. How many players are on court altogether?
exercises.hint: Two teams of 7: add or double.
exercises.explain: Each netball team has 7 players on court, so 7 + 7 = 14 players. In football there are 11 a side, so 11 + 11 = 22 players.

exercises.hint: Think of stepping in front of a pass.
choices: catching a pass meant for the other team
exercises.explain: An interception is catching or stopping a pass meant for a player on the other team. Watch the ball, step in front as it is thrown, and now your team is attacking.

exercises.prompt: In basketball, you move with the ball by bouncing it as you go: dribbling.
exercises.hint: Can you run with the ball in basketball if you bounce it?
exercises.explain: True: bouncing the ball as you move is dribbling.

exercises.prompt: Match each invasion game to how you move with the ball.
matches: you may not run with it
exercises.hint: Every game has its own rules for moving with the ball.
exercises.explain: In netball you may not run with the ball; in basketball you bounce it as you go; in football you kick it along; in rugby you carry it as you run.

exercises.prompt: Your team wins the ball. Put a good attack in order.
items: Shoot when you are close to goal.
Look up for a teammate in space.
Pass, then move into a new space.
Intercept a pass from the other team.
exercises.hint: First you need the ball. Then keep it, move it forward and score.
exercises.explain: Intercept to win the ball, look up for a teammate in space, pass and move to keep it and get closer, then shoot when you are near the goal.
